*Name:* <https://app.gohighlevel.com/v2/location/<crm-id-10>/contacts/detail/<crm-id-26>|<contact-17> Aguayo>
*Recording:* <<url-6>>
*Appointment:* Tue Oct 20 · 11:00 AM PDT · marked showed
*Closer:* <staff-4> · 47 min

*Outcome:* follow up
*Pain:* 
• "the people that I've been, um, I feel like attracting have been people that I need to kind of mother or help in some type of way"
• "I just haven't met that, that, that interesting person for me"
• "I don't know if these apps are actually helping out or some type of algorithm"
• "I will say maybe like 3% that I will date. Everything else is just, I don't, I don't even bother."
• "I think it will be more of someone that I feel is financially stable, like I am."
• "I feel like I end up being a little bit, a little bit more like smarter in a way"
• "I don't know if it's me traveling so much and not being in one city in order to meet someone"
• "Maybe I've just been so submerged of working so much that I didn't put myself out there."
• On apps: "I am skeptical, but I still use them."
*Goal:* 
• "I want to have children. I want to get married. I want a meaningful relationship. I want to create memories."
• "someone that is inspiring to me... family oriented, that wants to travel, do things together... that will share values, um, and beliefs to a certain extent"
• "I need to have that emotional connection with that person."
• "I would like to meet someone who's already ready... A partnership."
• Timeline for marriage: "within six months, three months". The speaker label is unclear here, but the follow-up suggests this was Nia's answer.
• "someone that inspires me and that it's, that is ready to like, he's ready to meet that person to have a family, and to just enjoy life"
*Objections:* 
• Needs to think about it
• Past program didn't work (she didn't engage)
• Money / competing priorities
• Unsure it will work
*Next Steps:* Nia will let <staff-3> know 'in the next few hours' whether she is moving forward. <staff-3> is holding the $3,000 spot until 4 p.m. Central (3 p.m. Pacific) the same day. Nia has <staff-3>'s number to text questions. If she joins, her one-on-one strategy call would ideally happen later this week, and the group starts in October.
✅ Showed · 47 min with <staff-4>. The review is in the calls channel.

*Scorecard:* 5/10
*Overall Score:* 5
*Scores:*
    *Rapport:* 7
    *Discovery:* 6
    *Pain Depth:* 4
    *Presentation:* 6
    *Objection Handling:* 4
    *Close Attempt:* 5
*Strengths:*
• Warm opener: she confirmed the name Nia vs. <contact-17> and asked which setter Nia spoke to.
• Sharp diagnostic question: 'is the issue you're not meeting men who want to commit to you, or you're not getting asked out, or... not meeting men who are successful enough?' Nia replied 'That's a very good question... I never questioned that to myself.' It surfaced the financial-stability criterion.
• Quantified her activity well (five dates in three months, mostly apps, 'maybe like 3%' worth dating). This gave concrete grounds for the pitch.
• Probed the past-program objection directly ('what was the promise with that versus what was delivered?'). This revealed the real issue: Nia never engaged ('it was me').
• Answered that objection with concrete low-friction fixes: a phone app and her personal number.
• Used a time-bound hold: the $3,000 spot held until 4 p.m. Central, with timezone confirmed and Nia agreeing it was 'enough time.'
*Misses:*
• Put words in Nia's mouth: 'I'm not getting any younger.' Nia pushed back: 'But I don't say I'm not getting any younger. I never use those... I don't use that type of wording.' This cost rapport right before the pitch.
• Fed back things Nia never said. She claimed 'like you even said, you're exhausted' and 'you lost five years with that.' Nia never said she was exhausted. This makes the diagnosis feel imposed rather than drawn from her.
• Missed a strong buying signal. Nia asked 'is this a package? How can we go about moving forward?' <staff-3> replied with a long price anchor ($10K–$100K clients) instead of moving to commitment.
• Pain stayed surface-level. The one-year future-pace question ('If a year from now, you're in the same place...') got a thin answer ('because I feel that I'm ready'). <staff-3> moved on instead of digging into what it costs Nia emotionally.
• The 'think about it' was never isolated. <staff-3> asked 'Is it purely about the money...?' and got 'a little bit of both' but didn't break that apart. When Nia mentioned 'other personal things,' <staff-3> didn't ask what they were.
• She repeated the 'what's your plan if you don't do this?' question twice and got 'I haven't thought of it' both times. Repeating it added pressure without moving her.
• Long monologue during the presentation. <staff-3> acknowledged it herself: 'I've been talking a lot.'
• No firm follow-up was set. 'Let me know in the next few hours' leaves the ball with the prospect. There was no scheduled callback before the 4 p.m. deadline.
*Coaching:*
• Mirror the prospect's exact words and never insert loaded phrases like 'I'm not getting any younger.' Before diagnosing, summarize only what she actually said and get a 'yes.'
• When a prospect asks 'how can we move forward?', give the price simply and ask for the decision. Save anchoring for later, or drop it.
• Isolate the stall. For example: 'If money weren't a factor, would you join today?' Then ask what the 'other personal things' are. Book a specific callback time before the hold expires (e.g., 2:30 p.m. Central) rather than waiting for her text.
*Talk Ratio:* Roughly 65–70% <staff-3> / 30–35% Nia. <staff-3> dominated the long diagnosis and pitch. Speaker labels in the transcript are frequently misattributed, so this is approximate.
